title: Block a command with a hook
intro: A PreToolUse hook on the Bash tool runs a small script before every shell command. The script blocks commands that start with rm. Type a command Claude might want to run and see what the hook decides.

show.title: Blocked by the hook
show.detail: The script saw a command starting with rm and exited with code 2. On PreToolUse, exit code 2 blocks the tool call, and the text the script wrote to standard error is the reason Claude receives.

trace.text: About to run a Bash command: {{command}}
Reads the event as JSON on standard input and extracts the command.
echo "Blocked: rm commands are not allowed" >&2; exit 2
Exit code 2: the tool call is prevented.
Receives the hook's message as the tool's error and can change its plan.

show.title: The hook lets it through
show.detail: The command does not start with rm, so the script exits with code 0. That is not an approval: the hook made no decision, and the normal permission flow applies.

trace.text: About to run a Bash command: {{command}}
Reads the event as JSON on standard input and extracts the command.
Exit code 0: the action continues with the usual permission checks.

fallback.title: Type a command first
fallback.detail: This demo only scripts one rule: commands that start with rm are blocked, and everything else passes. Enter a command to see which case applies.

quiz.question: A PreToolUse hook must stop a tool call. Which exit code does that?
quiz.explanation: Exit code 2 is the blocking error. Exit code 0 means success, and any other code is a non-blocking error: the action normally goes ahead.
